messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered: P1 - KV cache exhaustion observed in rope-serving pool (alerts: high mem, token-latency-spike)

alex (oncall): getting paged, looking now. seeing lots of OOM-ish logs on rope nodes. UI shows 5xx spikes for embeddings/long-context requests.

alex (oncall): @samir can you confirm any recent deploys touching NTK/YaRN scaling or sliding-window?

samir (runtime): I pushed a routing tweak yesterday to prefer NTK-long for >32k tokens, and a YaRN sliding_window param increase for throughput. Rollout was gradual but may've changed cache hit patterns.

maria (sre): hmm that would cause KV cache miss amplification. logs show continuous-batching queues growing and kv cache key cardinality up 12x in last 20m.

alex (oncall): spike timeline: 09:12 UTC start, ramped until 09:26. Impact: several customers reported 10-15s tail latencies then 502s.

ella (cust-succ): FYI @support we already got 3 pages from Enterprise A about timeouts. Telling them we're investigating and will update in 15.

samir (runtime): quick mitigation idea: revert NTK-long routing or clamp long-context routing to preserve prefix sharing; and temporarily disable continuous batching for rope pool so KV gets stabilized.

maria (sre): agree. also limit per-request sliding_window size (YaRN) to previous value to reduce churn. I'm going to run a controlled hotfix: set batch.max_tokens=2048 and yarn.sliding_window=0.6 -> previous was 0.9.

alex (oncall): commands I'm running now:
```
# limit batch size so continuous batching doesn't aggregate huge sequences
redwoodctl runtime apply-config --pool rope-serving --set batch.max_tokens=2048
# clamp routing for long-context models to avoid NTK-long for unknown clients
redwoodctl routing update --policy rope --set prefer_ntk_long=false
# reduce YaRN window fraction
redwoodctl runtime apply-config --pool rope-serving --set yarn.sliding_window=0.6
```

infra-bot: Config apply started (change-id: cfg-20240315-842). Rolling to 12 nodes in pool rope-serving.

maria (sre): also kicking off a KV cache flush for affected namespace to evict pathological keys: `kvctl flush --namespace=rope-ntk-transient --confirm`

alex (oncall): flush command went through. watching mem and key-cardinality.

(2m later)
alex (oncall): CPU and mem dropping on 7 of 12 nodes, batch queues shrinking. 5xx rate down from 18% -> 3%. latency p50 stable, p95 falling.

ella (cust-succ): messaging update for customers: "We've applied a mitigation and are seeing error rates fall; engineering is continuing to monitor. We'll follow up with a root cause and timeline by EOD."

samir (runtime): preliminary root cause: the NTK-long routing change caused a subset of requests to bypass prefix KV sharing (long-context requests get distinct rolling keys), and the YaRN sliding window increase broadened batch scopes so the KV cache saw many unique ephemeral keys. Combined, key cardinality exploded and continuous batching attempted to materialize huge batches causing memory pressure and perf cliffs.

maria (sre): logging notes: had ~2m sustained contiguous OOM retries; autoscaler kicked but nodes were too hot. Hotfix rolled out at 09:34 UTC.

alex (oncall): status: mitigation applied, error rate down, customer impact reduced. I'm going to keep the incident thread open and handoff to maria for follow-up and postmortem.

maria (sre): taking over. I'm creating a follow-up ticket to revert the NTK-long rollout until we have evals for KV-sharing impact and add telemetry for per-key churn.

samir (runtime): action items I will own:
- revert NTK-long gradual rollout and add a canary that checks KV key churn
- add a hard cap to continuous-batching memory per-request
- add an emergency toggle to disable YaRN sliding_window expansion

ell a (cust-succ): I'll coordinate with affected customers for a postmortem summary and share timelines.

incident-bot: Incident P1 (id: P1-20240315-64) transitioned to MITIGATED by alex at 09:38 UTC.

maria (sre): follow-up tasks created: RED-3561 (revert routing), RED-3562 (kv telemetry), RED-3563 (automatic batch caps). Scheduling RCA meeting tomorrow 11:00 UTC.

alex (oncall): handoff complete, leaving channel. ping me if hotfix reverts or another spike. :thumbsup:

maria (sre): thanks. filing a brief timeline for the postmortem:
- 09:12 - first alerts (mem & latency)
- 09:18 - oncall paged, initial triage
- 09:22 - identified high KV key churn and continuous-batching backlog
- 09:26 - suspected NTK/YaRN rollout correlation
- 09:30 - applied config hotfixes (batch clamp, routing clamp, yarn window)
- 09:34 - KV flush executed
- 09:38 - error rates dropped to acceptable thresholds, incident mitigated

maria (sre): tagging owners and next steps in ticket. postmortem will include test harness to simulate long-context workload (NTK/YaRN combo) and a gating requirement for future sliding_window or routing changes.

incident-bot: Postmortem checklist created: PM assigned = ella, RCA meeting scheduled.

maria (sre): closing thread for now, will attach logs and grep outputs in RED-3561.

ella (cust-succ): thank you team — I'll send customer updates once RCA draft is ready.

samir (runtime): adding a note to model onboarding docs: any long-context routing changes must include KV-churn simulation and cost modeling.

alex (oncall): final: please add an emergency runbook step to clamp batch.max_tokens and flush rope KV as mitigation for memory storms.

maria (sre): will add to runbook.

(End of thread)
